checksums.name: candidate_header_checksum
checksums.formula_detail: FUN_080219ee (ghidra/decompiled.c) is structurally an Adler-32 variant: A=1,B=0; per byte A=A+byte, B=B+A; periodic modulo reduction via FUN_080283a0 (compiler reciprocal-multiply mod, modulus unresolved from decompiled C); return (B<<16)|A. No traced caller/callee edge exists for this function in ghidra/callgraph.json, and no tested byte-range/endianness/modulus combination reproduces the stored bytes at offset 0x0-0x3 in saves/cap-01-future-1.sav. Treated as an unverified structural candidate only.

io_driver_functions.notes: Low-level DMA3 register programmer (src/dst/control) + busy-wait, used by both the EEPROM read and write primitives to drive the serial bus.
EEPROM single 8-byte block READ: builds READ-opcode+address bitstream, DMAs it out to 0x0D000000, DMAs back 64 data bits, deserializes into caller buffer. MMIO seed function.

EEPROM single 8-byte block WRITE: builds WRITE-opcode+address+64-bit-payload bitstream, DMAs it to 0x0D000000, polls EEPROM write-busy bit via paired IRQ-guard helpers 0x08021e30/0x08021eb8. MMIO seed function.
Interrupt-state guard entered immediately before the EEPROM write-busy poll (BIOS Intr-wait-style jump table).
Paired interrupt-state restore, entered immediately after the write-busy poll resolves.
Read-back verify: reads one block via 0x08021f7c and compares against the caller's write buffer; returns 0x8000 on mismatch.
Block write-with-retry wrapper: write (0x0802202c) + verify (0x08022108), retry up to 3 times. No traced caller in ghidra/callgraph.json; likely called from un-traced game-logic save code.
Load-all entry point: selects EEPROM backup type, allocates an 8192-byte heap buffer, reads all 1024 blocks via 0x08021f7c into it. No traced caller.

Save entry point: flushes a caller-specified byte range of the RAM mirror to EEPROM, one 8-byte block at a time, via 0x08022160. Byte-count parameter is caller-controlled, consistent with only block 0 having been flushed in the observed samples. No traced caller.
Sets up the same transfer-descriptor fields as 0x08021974's tail but contains no write loop of its own; hypothesized deferred/async write-descriptor setup. Unverified, no caller/callee edges traced.

caller_chains.trigger_context: Unknown game event (no traced caller); presumably a continue/load-save menu action.
ram_fields_updated: dynamic heap buffer at *_DAT_08021a48 (8192 bytes, full save mirror)
caller_chains.how_mapped: Traced by reading FUN_08021904 in ghidra/decompiled.c: calls func_0x08021d90(0x40) to select EEPROM backup type, FUN_0801f53c(0x2000) to allocate the RAM mirror, FUN_0802106a to program the DMA control word, then loops func_0x08021f7c once per 8-byte block for all 1024 blocks (0..0x2000 step 8), confirmed to match the 8192-byte EEPROM size from saves/*.sav.

caller_chains.trigger_context: Unknown game event (no traced caller); byte-range parameter (param_4) is caller-controlled. Observed .sav evidence implies the actual call(s) that produced saves/cap-01-future-1.sav used param_4 ~= 8 (only block 0 written).

caller_chains.how_mapped: Traced by reading FUN_08021974: loops func_0x08022160 (write+verify+retry) once per 8-byte block across the caller-supplied byte range, then restores DMA state via FUN_08021080. Cross-checked against saves/hexdump_and_diffs.txt showing exactly 8 changed bytes (one block) between cap-00 and cap-01.

fields.name: block0_header_candidate
fields.update_mechanism: Flushed as the first half of EEPROM block 0 via the write-with-retry primitive (0x08022160); no field-level writer code was captured in-trace, so the exact in-RAM producer of this value is unknown.
fields.evidence: Only non-fill bytes besides offset 4-7; candidate checksum per the structural Adler-32 match of FUN_080219ee, but no tested formula/window reproduces this exact value (see checksums[0].verified_on_samples).

fields.name: block0_payload_candidate

fields.evidence: Low-magnitude byte values (0,4,6,4) plausible as small counters/flags; no semantic label can be assigned without further gameplay-correlated samples.

fuzzing_targets.predicted_effect: If offset 0x0-0x3 is a validated checksum, the game should either reject/reset the block or overwrite it with a freshly computed value on next save; if it is ordinary data, no corrective reaction should occur.
Any observable HUD/menu/state change would begin to assign semantics to these 4 bytes; requires paired pre/post .ss states, which are not currently present in states/ for this release.

fuzzing_targets.mutation: write a non-0xFF byte into the currently-unwritten tail
fuzzing_targets.predicted_effect: Determines whether block 1+ is live-but-unused-so-far versus structurally dead space; a subsequent real game save overwriting this byte back would indicate the former.

open_questions: Is offset 0x0-0x3 actually a checksum, and if so over what range/algorithm/modulus/endianness? FUN_080219ee is a structural Adler-32 candidate but is unverified and has no traced caller in ghidra/callgraph.json.
What do bytes at offset 0x4-0x7 represent semantically?
Does this title use more than one save slot or a backup/mirrored copy elsewhere in the 8192-byte EEPROM? Not observed in either of the 2 available samples.
Is there a sequence/generation counter governing slot selection? Not observed (only a single write event visible across both samples).
Which game-logic call sites invoke 0x08021904 (load) and 0x08021974 (save)? Both have zero traced callers in ghidra/callgraph.json.
What is the role of 0x080219d6 (descriptor-setup-only, no write loop) relative to 0x08021974 -- deferred/async write path, or unused/dead code?
